notes:
**Print, Stop, Abort.** The Pause button is gone from the Print page: Print starts a run and continues a stopped one, Stop finishes the pieces already in the printer and runs the machine's pause routine, and Abort halts and flushes. After a Stop, pressing Print carries on where the run left off; changing which records to print starts a fresh run instead.

**The run-complete window is a proper report.** It shows the printing time (first piece to last piece) separately from the whole run time, so a feeder started late is not charged against the rate, and adds a cost breakdown: ink from the printer's own drop count at your cartridge price, stock at a per-piece cost, and the total with a per-1,000 figure. Both prices can be changed right there and are kept — the cartridge price machine-wide, the stock cost with the job (it also lives on the Studio page's Media section, where "Use machine default" puts it back). Untick a line to leave it out of the total.

**Feeder control is a machine setting.** Settings ▸ Machine now says how this machine pauses its feeder: through VP Link, through a XiJet relay (which relay, and whether energised means paused or running), or not at all. VP Studio uses that whenever it needs the feeder to wait, and the Print page says plainly when it cannot reach a feeder.

**Pause the feeder at every batch or sort break.** "Pause The Feeder" joins blank pieces and the relay pulse as a separator, for a set number of seconds or until you click the Print button, which reads "Paused — click to resume" while it waits — a way to batch by hand. The machine default is set in Settings ▸ Printing, which is now the one place for batch defaults; the separate File ▸ Batch Options window is gone, and each job's own separator is still set from the Print page.

**The installer recognises your machine.** It lists TNR's machine models, reads the print head and proposes the matching one, and fills the setup from that model's baseline. Settings ▸ Machine shows the model and offers "Match against the machine list…" for a machine set up before this, and carries the distance from the transport entry to the print sensor, which tells Studio how many pieces are committed on the belt when the feeder stops.

**Mock mode keeps time.** The simulated belt now fires at exactly the interval you set (200 ms is 18,000 pieces an hour), its preview no longer slows it, and the mock preview is a faithful copy of what the printer receives.

**Data files that are not quite CSV open.** A file whose records end in a bare carriage return used to load as a single row of columns, and a file with no header row became zero records with the first record's text as the field names. Both load now: Studio notices a missing header row and names the fields Field1, Field2…, and the Data page's source band gains a "First row is field names" switch that shows what was decided and lets you change it — the answer is saved with the job. An XML file holding a single record loads with the same field names a multi-record file gives. Loading a different data file clears the printed marks, which belonged to the old rows, and says so.

**Every barcode is checked before you print.** Check Layout now runs each record's barcode data through the encoder and flags "Barcode won't encode" with the reason, so a record that would have printed red text where the bars should be is caught in the list, not in the stack. On the Data page, Data quality no longer goes quiet when a numeric field has a few values that are not digits — it names them with a show link — and judges an Intelligent Mail field by the four lengths USPS allows.

**Clearer when the belt is not moving.** The message that used to say only "the transport isn't moving" now also covers a belt that is turning while the printer's encoder reports nothing, and says what to check. The companion no longer reports a lost connection to the print service as a crash, and its error records show the suite version.

**TNR Developments is at www.tnrdevelopments.com.** Ordering, licence requests, error reports and diagnostics go there now; older installs keep working through the previous address until they update.
